default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-1308.title: VWAP slope pullback
E-1308.hypothesis: When the session VWAP is rising unusually fast, institutional buyers benchmarked to VWAP defend it; a dip touching VWAP that closes back above is a continuation entry (mirrored for sells).

E-1309.title: Bar-gap vacuum fade
E-1309.hypothesis: A bar whose whole range lies beyond the previous bar's range crossed an empty book; the overshoot tends to be partly given back, so fade the gap bar.

E-1310.title: Rolling VWAP cross follow
E-1310.hypothesis: A close that moves away from the volume-weighted average price of the last N minutes shows recent volume is being done at worse prices for the other side; follow the cross.

E-1312.title: Gap-fill midpoint continuation
E-1312.hypothesis: After an opening gap, positioning from the prior session is trapped; once price retraces half the gap early in the session, the fill toward yesterday's close tends to be completed.

E-1314.title: Large-bar dip in trend
E-1314.hypothesis: In a trend (price on one side of a slow EMA) a single oversized counter-trend bar is mostly a liquidity flush by weak hands; trade back with the trend at its close.

E-1315.title: Outside bar strong close
E-1315.hypothesis: A bar that takes out both the previous high and low and closes near one end has cleared stops on both sides and shown who won; follow the close.

E-1316.title: Wick pressure accumulation
E-1316.hypothesis: A rolling excess of lower over upper wicks shows sellers repeatedly rejected by resting bids (or the reverse); follow the side that keeps defending.

E-1317.title: Opening-range midpoint cross
E-1317.hypothesis: After the opening range is set, its midpoint is the balance point; a close crossing it shows the auction leaning to that side, so follow each crossing.
